record.original_question: In Gilbert's high-low search game, Blue chooses a secret number h, after each guess tells Red whether the guess is too high, too low, or correct, and may then change the secret number provided the new choice remains consistent with all previous answers. If V(n) is the value of the n-number game, is it true that V(n) - log2(n) converges to a constant c as n→∞, with c approximately 0.487?

evidence.quote: Dresher’s guessing game has recently been solved asymptotically [8], but there is a very similar high-low search game that remains unsolved. It was proposed around the same time as Dresher’s game, by Ed Gilbert [ 12]. As in Dresher’s game, Blue chooses a secret number h and tells Red whether his guess is too high, too low, or correct. However, after doing this, Blue may change the secret number, but it has to be in accordance with the answers that have been given so far.

This recursion should make the game easier to solve. It certainly makes the value of the game easier to compute, and it is conjectured in [7] that the value of the game satisﬁes lim n→∞ V (n)−log2(n)= c for some constant c = 0.487 ... .

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following two-player zero-sum search game with parameter $n \geq 1$. Blue secretly maintains a number $h \in \{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$. In each round, Red announces a guess $g \in \{1,\ldots,n\}$, and Blue must truthfully answer "too high", "too low", or "correct" relative to some value $h$, but Blue is allowed to change $h$ between rounds as long as every answer given so far remains consistent with at least one fixed sequence of valid choices (equivalently, Blue maintains the set $S$ of remaining candidates; on a guess $g$, Blue chooses one of the responses "high", "low", or "correct" and updates $S$ to $\{x \in S : x < g\}$, $\{x \in S : x > g\}$, or $\{g\}$ respectively). The game ends when Red identifies the unique remaining value; the payoff to Blue (and the loss to Red) is the number of guesses Red used. Both players play optimally. Let $V(n)$ denote the value of this game starting from $S = \{1,\ldots,n\}$.

Determine whether
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\bigl(V(n) - \log_2 n\bigr) = c$$
exists, and whether $c \approx 0.487$.
artifact.status_search_result: Public search results indicate that Gilbert's high–low search game with a mutable secret remains studied as an unsolved problem, with the asymptotic behavior of V(n) − log₂ n stated as a conjecture rather than a theorem. No source found establishing the limit or the value c ≈ 0.487.

status_evidence.title: A High–Low search game on the unit interval
status_evidence.snippet: Academic work on high-low search games with logarithmic value behavior; no resolution of Gilbert's discrete game asymptotic constant reported.
status_evidence.claim: The asymptotic constant for Gilbert's high-low search game has not been established in the accessible literature.
